parsed.explanation: Visitors face low border/document risk: visa nationality-only; officially issued non-birth or X passports accepted; no extra gender documents. Accommodation discrimination is prohibited and Pride safety coordination exists, with high trans-acceptance reducing ordinary exposure. The main severe conditional exposure is custody: no governing placement rule, male/female separation via municipal gender plus physical features, frequent Extra Care wings shared with sex offenders/disabled, and documented male-wing intimidation/assault history. Remedies are uneven: rising reports, few convictions, unresolved hate-crime coverage, unpublished guidelines. Minors and care-specific visitor risks are not documented. Overall safe for routine travel, materially lowered by institutional custody gap.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No reported visa refusal, border questioning, marker rejection, extra gender documents, or passport-mismatch penalty for visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Visa depends on nationality; officially issued passports with non-birth or X markers accepted; no additional gender documents demanded at border.
entry_documents.interaction: Removes primary outing point; local/federal entry rules are aligned, so visitor documents are not forced into local gender process.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Custody has no placement law; municipal gender and case-by-case features decide; frequent Extra Care wings alongside sex offenders/disabled; documented male-wing intimidation, threats, assaults and molestation before transfers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Court rulings call mismatched placement heavy; transfers occur; police record discrimination. No operative national guideline.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention or fraud investigation could turn document mismatch or discovery into severe placement harm; protections do not cancel custody risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No reported birth-sex facility ban, hotel refusal, bathroom denial or checkpoint exclusion against visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Accommodation and services discrimination prohibited on gender identity/expression/sex characteristics; bathroom access recorded protected; Pride safer-spaces points.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor-facing facility rules align with protections; no documented local exception at entry or hotels.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No reported traveler-specific emergency-care refusal, hormone/HRT denial, ward-mismatch or insurance gatekeeping.
care_services.protection: Not documented for visitors. Youth-care recommendations and conversion-therapy ban are resident climate, not traveler protections.
care_services.interaction: Health emergencies may expose records, but no operative visitor care restriction is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Government victimisation reports say 17% of trans people faced physical/sexual violence; reports and Pride incidents rose, including serious assault; only six convictions and no background comparator.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: High trans acceptance, anti-discrimination law, bias-motive penalty mechanism, dedicated discrimination-recording police unit, no state demonization documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law supports visitors, but hostility and enforcement gaps can make reporting and remedy uneven.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No reported family outing, guardian refusal, school placement or child custody rule affecting trans minors travelling.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented for visitors. National youth-care support is climate only.
minors_guardians.interaction: If guardian and minor enter custody, adult placement gap could extend to dependent; minor facility practice not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Pride/platform reports include insults, theft, vandalism, intimidation and serious assault; trans reports rose 264 to 399; perpetrators often flee; reports may be a fraction.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No police raids, profiling or extortion documented; safer-spaces reporting points, mayoral priority, police-enforcer agreements.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police record and respond, but low convictions and unpublished guidelines leave street-victim remedy uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gender-identity coverage of penalty enhancement unresolved; no statutory hate-crime definition; only six convictions; custody guidelines unpublished; no trans detainee counts; prevalence lacks denominator.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Complaints through police discrimination unit; victims rights; courts recognized heavier mismatched custody; accommodation law.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Protective remedies may work outside custody, but unknowns persist where discovery triggers investigation or detention.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar broad equality-law climate and functional policing, but lower because custody is a serious state practice gap with sex-offender/disabled wings and documented assault, unlike 0.85-A where issues are isolated rural/shelter hesitancy and protections generally operate.

Above 0.75-D on border acceptance and high public trans support, but below on custody: 0.75-D attacks can be prosecuted with protective orders; here detention placement can impose severe harm with no governing rule and weak remedy.

Above 0.65-A because 0.65-A has document-mismatch detentions and bureaucratic friction; here entry accepts X/passport markers and no extra docs. Custody remains more severe than ordinary friction, but the overall visitor regime is safer.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime protects entry and public accommodation but contains a severe institutional custody gap. A visitor is unlikely to encounter forced disclosure at borders and may use venues under anti-discrimination rules. However, if arrested, birth-record/physical-feature placement and Extra Care with sex offenders/disabled can impose major harm, with only case-by-case transfers and no published rule. Social hostility is visible through Pride and report rises, but not state-directed; high acceptance and police reporting temper it. Low convictions and unclear gender-identity penalty coverage limit remedy.
